report:
Reviewed the complete generated_identity claim, all four ordinary implementation associations, both ordinary tests, and the explicit TODO test. The requirements are: generated source identity contains stable input, generating operation and occurrence; generated text and current origin coordinates remain changeable facts outside that identity; moving the origin neither merges distinct occurrences nor creates a replacement identity. In derive.rs the interned DeriveExpansion includes source_item, macro_def, derive_name, attribute_index and derive_index, with neither text nor coordinates among its keys. origin reads the current source-item span, text invokes a tracked output query, and parse_output is tracked by the expansion identity. In local_syms/mods.rs attribute enumeration and within-list enumeration are propagated through expand_derive into those interning keys. Thus same-name derives at separate list or attribute occurrences remain distinct, and the resolved generating operation participates in identity. In span.rs ParseSource distinguishes file, BangMacro(definition, invocation), and Derive(expansion); byte ranges are separate AbsoluteSpan fields. In local_syms/macro_invocations.rs a tracked invocation has mutable CST/span fields and parse_output is keyed by invocation and macro definition; generated text is recomputed from the current tokens and passed separately to parsing. Nested expansion recurses through these same source representations and tracked parse-output boundaries. Added essential associations for these three previously unassociated implementation files, then started a fresh review.

The duplicate_derive_occurrences_have_distinct_generated_source_identity test creates two Clone occurrences on the same item, obtains both actual emitted impl sources, asserts there are exactly two, asserts unequal expansion identities, and checks occurrence indices zero and one. It would detect removing the occurrence discriminator from the interning identity. moving_source_item_preserves_derive_expansion_identity edits the same SourceFile by prepending a newline, forces expansion again, and asserts equal raw expansion IDs but unequal current origin starts. It would detect coordinate-keyed identities and stale origin facts. Captured fixture setup constructs the actual root module in a tracked query; BuiltinDeriveTcx supplies Clone macro resolution, so these assertions exercise expansion rather than manually fabricated identities.

The TODO types_spans_generated_identity is intentionally empty and supplies no runtime assurance. Its comment explicitly retains missing nested expansion identity/text/origin/coordinate comparisons. This is accepted as a visible test deferral: the prerequisite for retiring it is a substantive revision-driven nested expansion fixture comparing generated identity, generated text and origin coordinates, including multiple occurrences and generating operations. Existing tests do not prove that broader matrix, text-change independence, or all bang-macro movement cases. Source inspection supports the representation, while those scenarios remain deferred rather than silently credited to the two derive tests. There are no N/A entries and no deferred implementation entry. No behavioral violation was identified.

Executed cargo fmt, cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib derive_expansion_tests:: -- --nocapture (29 passed, including both associated ordinary tests), and cargo build (passed with existing compiler warnings). The TODO test was not run and would not verify behavior if run. Commands and source inspection are separate evidence. Required post-codegen and Sage sanity review of the association-only edits is coordinated centrally by root, as authorized in the captured instructions.
